version: 1.0 (Phase 3I, declared before the first manual run)
status_of_this_document: DECLARED BEFORE THE MANUAL RUN. Comparison plan for the two exploratory families of the archived V1.4 programme that the deposited record lists as ANOM (7,080 daily-reference anomaly models) and ALT (312 alternative exposure-history tests), plus two supporting frozen tables (anomaly diagnostics, 64 rows; trajectory-PCA variance, 439 rows). Numerical reproduction and independent verification are separate statuses. Nothing here is derived from a result of this run. The families are EXPLORATORY and separate from primary inference, from the nine final L01-L56 models (V2.1), from the archived DLMs (Phase 3E), the cold-burden scan (Phase 3F) and the daily-lag layer (Phase 3H). Horizons are kept as traced: ANOM windows 1-59 days (archived L01-L59); ALT histories use lags 1-56 (the original reads 59 lags but uses 56).

scope.anom: WINTER_CODE R/120_daily_anomaly.R siecc_participant_day_long, siecc_daily_anomaly_values, siecc_anomaly_diagnostics, siecc_build_anomaly_feature, siecc_daily_anomaly_scan; stage 14_daily_reference_anomaly_scan
scope.alt: WINTER_CODE R/130_alternative_methods.R siecc_history_matrix, siecc_row_aggregate, siecc_disjoint_features, siecc_weighted_feature, siecc_trajectory_contrasts, siecc_fit_multiexposure_joint, siecc_alternative_method_scan; stage 15_alternative_exposure_history_methods
scope.text_support: The manuscript (SIECC_Manuscript_Methods_Results_2809.docx) does not describe either family. SI Table S5 part C lists their multiplicity families only: anomaly scan 59 (lags within a fixed anomaly curve) / 2,360 (all tests within outcome) / 7,080 (complete scan); alternative methods 104 (features within outcome) / 312 (complete grid); SI Table S7 mentions anomaly and alternative-history q families as family-specific. These sizes agree with the traced code (q_curve, q_outcome, q_global). Neither document defines the reference, the anomaly scale or the features; the specification below is therefore traced from the V1.4 code and the frozen outputs, not from the text.
scope.kept_separate_from: primary inference; the nine final L01-L56 DLMs; archived L01-L59 DLM and lag-form sensitivity (Phase 3E); cold burden (Phase 3F); daily-lag layer XYD / DAY / MAXT (Phase 3H); no result of this family is combined with another

ANOM.grid: 2 reference definitions (all, locality) x 8 metrics x anomaly methods x 2 burden directions x 59 windows x 3 outcomes = 7,080. The methods are traced, not inferred from the count: every metric has the stable anomaly (the original assigns it through the metric's domain: thermal and moisture); the two rainfall metrics (IMS_rainfall_total, IMS_rainy_day_count_ge_1_mm; domain moisture) additionally have the zero-safe log anomaly. 6 x 1 + 2 x 2 = 10 metric-method combinations x 2 references x 2 burdens x 59 x 3 = 7,080 (frozen file: 1,416 stable rows and 354 zero-safe rows per reference and burden).
ANOM.order: reference (all, locality), metric (configuration order), method (stable, then zero-safe for the rainfall metrics), burden (signed_mean, absolute_mean), window 1..59, outcome
ANOM.exposure_history: the daily field <prefix>_L01..L59 of each metric (participant x lag). The calendar axis is calendar_date = assessment_date - lag. The package's canonical data hold assessment_day (days since the first assessment, 29 January 2026; the manuscript and SI Table S2 define it so), a fixed offset of the date, so assessment_day - lag groups participant-days exactly as the date does; the one-to-one correspondence of day and date is by definition (the audited SAV shows 33 distinct values of each) and is not verifiable from the canonical CSV: it is tested indirectly by the frozen anomaly diagnostics (min, max, 1st and 99th percentile of all participant-day anomalies per metric, method and reference).
ANOM.reference_definition: for each participant-day, the reference is the mean of the other participants' values of the same metric on the same calendar day (leave-one-out): all = every participant; locality = participants of the same Locality_3group. total = sum of finite values of the group, n = number of finite values; reference_mean_loo = (total - value) / (n - 1) for a finite value in a group with n >= 2, otherwise NA (a participant who is alone in a calendar-day x locality group has no reference). reference_sd = SD of the group's finite values (n >= 2).
ANOM.anomaly_scales: stable_anomaly = (value - reference_mean_loo) / pooled_within_day_sd, where pooled_within_day_sd is the SD of all finite residuals (value - reference_mean_loo) of the metric over all participants and lags (one scale per metric and reference); zero_safe_log_anomaly (rainfall metrics only) = log1p(value) - log1p(reference_mean_loo); literal_ratio = (value - loo) / loo and daily_z = (value - loo) / reference_sd are computed and summarised in the diagnostics but not used in any model.
ANOM.features: for window W and burden: over lags 1..W, available = number of finite anomalies; the feature is NA if available < ceiling(0.8 x W); otherwise the mean of the anomalies (signed_mean) or of their absolute values (absolute_mean) with NA removed. No other transformation or standardisation: the model exposure is the raw feature.
ANOM.model: outcome ~ feature + M2_L covariates (Sex, Age, AssessmentDay_centered, Locality_3group, Econ_STS); complete cases on outcome, covariates and feature; gaussian OLS with HC3 inference (UCLA_Lonliness_SCORE, Isolation_cont) and ordinary maximum-likelihood logistic regression with Wald inference (Int_dummy; glm epsilon 1e-8, maxit 25) in the validated engine, with the 13 design and influence diagnostics. The original also runs a Firth fit for the binary outcome, but no Firth column is part of the frozen output and none is compared. transformation = '<reference>:<method>:<burden>', exposure = '.__anomaly', exposure_unit = 'daily_reference_anomaly', primary_role = 'EXPLORATORY_DAILY_ANOMALY'.
ANOM.missing_data: supplied missing daily values are kept missing (never imputed); a missing value is excluded from the reference and gives a missing anomaly; with the locality reference a singleton group gives n = 54 in the frozen models (1,620 of 7,080 rows have n = 54, all in the locality reference).
ANOM.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg over finite nominal p values: q_global over all 7,080; q_outcome within outcome (3 x 2,360); q_curve over the 59 windows within outcome x metric x reference x method x burden (120 families of 59).
ANOM.diagnostics_table: daily_anomaly_diagnostics.csv: for each reference (all, locality), metric and method (literal_ratio, daily_z, stable_anomaly, zero_safe_log_anomaly): n_total, n_finite, missing_fraction, minimum, maximum, 1st and 99th percentile (type 7) of the participant-day values; 64 rows.

ALT.grid: 8 metrics x 3 outcomes x 13 tests = 312: one three-period joint test (recent 1-7, intermediate 8-28, remote 29-56 days), five weighted cumulative features (half-life 3, 7, 14, 28 days and uniform over 56 days), four trajectory contrasts (overall_mean, recent_minus_remote, linear_lag_contrast, curvature_contrast) and, when the PCA can be computed, the first three principal components of the 56-day history.
ALT.order: metric (configuration order), outcome, then joint, five weighted, four contrasts, PC1-PC3
ALT.history: lags 1..56 of the metric's daily field (the original reads 59 and uses 56). Aggregation of the disjoint periods follows the metric: mean for temperature and humidity metrics, sum for the two rainfall metrics (configuration 'aggregation'); NA only if no value is finite; no 80% rule for the disjoint periods.
ALT.joint_test: the three period aggregates are each z-scored (sample SD, NA if the SD is 0) and entered together with the M2_L covariates; the test is the joint test of the three terms against the covariate-only model on complete cases: gaussian F test from the residual sums of squares (df1 = 3, df2 = residual df of the full model); binary outcome likelihood-ratio chi-square on 3 df from ordinary glm fits. effect is NA; n is the complete-case count.
ALT.weighted_cumulative: weights 0.5^((lag - 1) / half_life) over lags 1..56 (equal weights for the uniform feature); the feature is NA if fewer than ceiling(0.8 x 56) = 45 lags are finite; otherwise the weighted mean over the finite lags. Fitted as a single exposure with the M2_L covariates in the validated engine (raw feature, no standardisation); effect = standardised_effect, p = nominal_p.
ALT.trajectory_contrasts: overall_mean = row mean (NA removed); recent_minus_remote = mean of lags 1-14 minus mean of lags 43-56; linear_lag_contrast = sum(x x linear) / sum(|linear| over finite lags) with linear = lag centred; curvature_contrast likewise with quadratic = linear^2 - mean(linear^2); no availability rule. Fitted as single exposures as above.
ALT.trajectory_pca: principal components of the 56 lag columns (centred and scaled) on participants with all 56 lags finite, if at least 20 such participants exist; scores of the first three components (NA for the other participants) are fitted as single exposures. The sign of a principal component is arbitrary (decided by the linear-algebra library); it is compared as it is and any sign difference is reported separately (alt_pca_sign_diagnostic.csv), never accepted silently. The component variance table (439 rows) is a supporting frozen output.
ALT.multiplicity: BH over finite p values: q_global over all 312, q_outcome within outcome (3 x 104). The SI's 104 / 312 agree.

tolerance.note: the existing deterministic-fit class of the configuration (cumulative_abs, cumulative_rel) as for the cumulative, cold-burden and daily-lag references; no new criterion is introduced; EXACT / WITHIN_TOLERANCE / DIFFERENT; unmatched, duplicate, blank, unclassified and non-finite mismatches fail

verification.ANOM: (1) whole grid: the anomaly values of both references recomputed cell by cell by an independent route (for every participant-day the mean of the other participants, no group totals) and the pooled scales, stable and zero-safe anomalies and the diagnostics table compared; (2) whole grid: every one of the 2 x 10 x 2 x 59 x 55 window features recomputed by a literal per-participant route; (3) whole grid: BH q_global, q_outcome and q_curve recomputed with p.adjust; (4) scale and inference identities of every model (package and frozen); (5) independent lm / glm refit of every model (declared coverage: every 1st of 7,080, parameter independent_refit_every_anom) compared at the cumulative tolerance class.
verification.ALT: (1) whole grid: the features recomputed by an independent route for every participant; (2) whole grid: independent lm / glm refit of all 288 single-feature models and an independent F or likelihood-ratio computation of all 24 joint tests; (3) the PCA variance fractions from an independent eigen decomposition of the correlation matrix and the absolute component scores; (4) BH q_global and q_outcome recomputed with p.adjust.

statuses.EXECUTION_STATUS: PASS only when the run completes
statuses.INPUT_PROVENANCE_STATUS: PASS only when all four reference files exist and match the declared SHA-256, bytes, counts, keys, columns and grids
statuses.ANOM_REPRODUCTION_STATUS: PASS only when ANOM_7080 and ANOMDIAG_64 are EXACT / WITHIN_TOLERANCE with every declared cell compared and every categorical item equal
statuses.ANOM_VERIFICATION_STATUS: PASS only when every independent check passes
statuses.ALT_REPRODUCTION_STATUS: PASS only when ALT_312 and ALTPCA_439 are EXACT / WITHIN_TOLERANCE with every declared cell compared (a sign difference of a principal component is a difference)
statuses.ALT_VERIFICATION_STATUS: PASS only when every independent check passes
statuses.COVERAGE_STATUS: PASS only when no record or cell is missing, duplicated, unmatched or unclassified and the compared-cell counts equal the declared counts
statuses.SOURCE_INTEGRITY_STATUS: PASS only when the package source fingerprint is unchanged during the run
